selection_boundary: No video file exists in the approved local source pack, and no external clip was fully verified for this specialist pass. Every section therefore keeps a visible GAP and a unique source-safe non-video pathway. No title, channel, video ID, thumbnail or link has been invented.
common_gap_reason: No verified local video or fully checked current external clip is available for this named section. Keep the video gap visible; do not substitute a generic clip.

sections.learning_purpose: Identify how technology, social change and economic conditions can reshape work.
sections.watch_for: Which change creates both an opportunity and a pressure for workers?

alternative.before: Read the adjacent theory and choose one change named there.
alternative.during: Record the change, one effect on work and one possible worker response.
alternative.after: Explain why the same change may affect workers differently.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which source detail supports your claimed effect?
alternative.alt_text: Text-based map linking a change in work to effects and worker responses.

sections.learning_purpose: Connect strengths, values and evidence to a provisional career decision.
sections.watch_for: What evidence would make a pathway choice more realistic rather than simply more attractive?

alternative.before: Select two plausible directions and four decision criteria.
alternative.during: Add source evidence and mark where evidence is still missing.
alternative.after: Write a provisional choice and one condition that could change it.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which criterion carried the most weight, and why?
alternative.alt_text: Decision matrix comparing two pathways with evidence, priorities and gaps.

sections.section_title: Managing change and building a sustainable working life
sections.learning_purpose: Recognise adaptation as a planned response rather than a failure of the original goal.
sections.watch_for: Which parts of the goal can stay stable when the route has to change?

alternative.before: Read a fictional pathway plan and its new constraint.
alternative.during: Mark what stays, what changes and what must be checked.
alternative.after: Set a review point and a credible alternative route.
alternative.evidence_prompt: How does the revision protect the original purpose?
alternative.alt_text: Timeline adapting a pathway after change while retaining its core purpose.

sections.learning_purpose: Trace how roles exchange information, authority and support.
sections.watch_for: Where could unclear responsibility interrupt the work?

alternative.before: Choose a fictional or public workplace role.
alternative.during: Map four relationships and label what each connection exchanges.
alternative.after: Identify one breakdown risk and a clarification point.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which connection is most important to effective participation?
alternative.alt_text: Role map showing workplace relationships, information and responsibility.

sections.learning_purpose: Separate known facts, uncertainty and a safe source of current direction.
sections.watch_for: At what point does the worker need to stop assuming and check?

alternative.before: Read the source-safe fictional situation and the adjacent theory.
alternative.during: Sort known information, checks needed and a safe next communication.
alternative.after: Explain why the nominated check is safer than guessing.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What local fact must be checked against your teacher’s current instructions?
alternative.alt_text: Scenario sorted into known information, checks and safe next communication.

sections.learning_purpose: Distinguish observable cultural signals from assumptions about individuals.
sections.watch_for: Which observable behaviour supports or undermines the stated workplace value?

alternative.before: Read three short workplace snapshots.
alternative.during: Sort stated values, observable behaviours and inferred effects.
alternative.after: Revise one inference so it stays grounded in observable evidence.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What can you conclude, and what would require more evidence?
alternative.alt_text: Evidence sort separating stated culture, observed behaviour and inference.

sections.learning_purpose: Read an opportunity for requirements, context and evidence expectations.
sections.watch_for: Which words signal evidence the applicant needs to provide?

alternative.before: Use a teacher-provided or redacted current opportunity.
alternative.during: Label required, desirable, contextual and action information.
alternative.after: Match each requirement to evidence available, weak or missing.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which gap has the clearest next action?
alternative.alt_text: Annotated opportunity identifying requirements and evidence gaps.

sections.learning_purpose: Turn a quality claim into a truthful claim-evidence-result response.
sections.watch_for: What detail makes a claim verifiable instead of generic?

alternative.before: Read a generic application claim.
alternative.during: Add a specific situation, action and result without exaggeration.
alternative.after: Remove one word that overstates the evidence and explain why.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What can the reader verify from the revised example?
alternative.alt_text: Application paragraph revised from a generic claim to specific evidence and result.

sections.learning_purpose: Plan, rehearse and revise a relevant evidence-based interview answer.
sections.watch_for: Where does the response move from description to evidence?

alternative.before: Identify the question purpose and select one honest example.
alternative.during: Draft a concise response with context, action and result.
alternative.after: Revise the final sentence so it directly answers the question.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which revision improved relevance most?
alternative.alt_text: Written interview response planned, checked for evidence and revised for relevance.

sections.learning_purpose: Select a communication channel by purpose, audience, urgency, privacy and record needs.
sections.watch_for: Which factor rules out an otherwise convenient channel?

alternative.before: Read five fictional workplace messages.
alternative.during: Choose a channel and justify it using two factors.
alternative.after: Name one suitable alternative and its trade-off.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which choice changed after considering privacy or record needs?
alternative.alt_text: Communication channel matrix comparing purpose, audience, urgency, privacy and records.

sections.section_title: Professional spoken, written and digital communication
sections.learning_purpose: Revise a message for clarity, tone, action and an appropriate record.
sections.watch_for: What does the receiver need to know, do or confirm?

alternative.before: Read an unclear fictional workplace message.
alternative.during: Mark audience, purpose, required action and missing context.
alternative.after: Rewrite it with a concise subject, respectful tone and clear next step.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which edit most reduces the chance of misunderstanding?
alternative.alt_text: Workplace message edited for purpose, tone, clarity and action.

sections.learning_purpose: Repair misunderstanding with neutral observation, clarification and an agreed next step.
sections.watch_for: Which wording describes the issue without labelling the person?

alternative.before: Read the fictional misunderstanding and identify the underlying need.
alternative.during: Write an initial response, then replace blame with neutral observation and a question.
alternative.after: Add a clear agreed next step and check-back point.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which wording change makes repair more likely?
alternative.alt_text: Conversation repair script changing blame into observation, clarification and next action.

sections.section_title: Team roles, trust and shared goals
sections.learning_purpose: Translate trust and shared goals into observable team behaviours.
sections.watch_for: What would the team actually see or hear when trust is working?

alternative.before: Choose one shared goal from a teacher-approved context.
alternative.during: Write four observable behaviours and one check-in method.
alternative.after: Replace one vague value with a behaviour the team can review.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which behaviour is easiest to observe fairly?
alternative.alt_text: Team charter linking a shared goal to observable trust behaviours.

sections.learning_purpose: Use evidence to define a problem, compare options and review a decision.
sections.watch_for: What evidence helps distinguish a symptom from the actual problem?

alternative.before: Read a low-risk fictional work problem.
alternative.during: Define the problem, compare three options and identify evidence.
alternative.after: Select an action and add a review trigger.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Why is the chosen action more defensible than the alternatives?
alternative.alt_text: Decision board defining a problem, comparing options and setting a review trigger.

sections.learning_purpose: Recognise enterprise skills as evidence-based actions in context rather than personality labels.
sections.watch_for: Which action creates value, reduces waste or improves a process?

alternative.before: Read three short authentic-work cases.
alternative.during: Identify the action, skill, evidence and beneficiary.
alternative.after: Rewrite one vague claim as an observable enterprise action.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What makes the action useful in this context?
alternative.alt_text: Case analysis linking enterprise skills to observable actions and value.

sections.learning_purpose: Classify commitments and communicate a realistic boundary.
sections.watch_for: Which commitment can move, and which priority does that protect?

alternative.before: Review the supplied week and identify essential recovery time.
alternative.during: Sort fixed, flexible and negotiable commitments.
alternative.after: Write one respectful boundary or renegotiation message.
alternative.evidence_prompt: How does the revised week remain realistic?
alternative.alt_text: Weekly commitments map distinguishing fixed, flexible and negotiable time.

sections.learning_purpose: Notice escalating pressure and choose a proportionate support step without diagnosing a person.
sections.watch_for: Which observable change suggests the plan or support needs review?

alternative.before: Read a fictional, non-clinical workload scenario.
alternative.during: Separate observable pressures, controllable actions and sources of support.
alternative.after: Write an early help-seeking sentence and a review point.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Why is the proposed support step proportionate and respectful?
alternative.alt_text: Scenario separating observable pressure, controllable actions and support options.

sections.section_title: Adapting plans across changing life stages
sections.learning_purpose: Preserve purpose while adapting a plan to changed circumstances.
sections.watch_for: What should stay stable, and what can change without abandoning the goal?

alternative.before: Read the original fictional plan and one changed circumstance.
alternative.during: Mark keep, revise, check and contact decisions.
alternative.after: Set a review date and alternative route.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which revision best protects the person's priorities?
alternative.alt_text: Plan adapted to a life-stage change with review and alternative route.

sections.learning_purpose: Read common pay-record fields and recognise values that require a current official source.
sections.watch_for: Which fields describe earnings, deductions, superannuation and the pay period?

alternative.before: Use a fictional or current official sample, never a student's real record.
alternative.during: Label field purpose and trace relationships shown in the sample.
alternative.after: Flag any rate or obligation that must be checked for currency.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which two fields would you verify first if something looked wrong?
alternative.alt_text: De-identified pay record annotated by field purpose and current-source checks.

sections.learning_purpose: Make a transparent budget trade-off and retain a buffer where possible.
sections.watch_for: Which expense is essential, flexible or deferrable in this fictional scenario?

alternative.before: Review the fictional budget and its stated priorities.
alternative.during: Apply one change, protect essentials and adjust two categories.
alternative.after: Explain the remaining consequence and review trigger.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What did you protect first, and why?
alternative.alt_text: Fictional budget revised after a change with priorities and consequences shown.

sections.section_title: Consumer decisions, risk and future planning
sections.learning_purpose: Compare consumer options by total commitment, uncertainty and future flexibility.
sections.watch_for: Which appealing feature distracts from the longer-term cost or risk?

alternative.before: Read two fictional offers with no current rates presented as fact.
alternative.during: Compare commitment, fees, flexibility, consequence and information gaps.
alternative.after: List the current official information needed before a real decision.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which uncertainty matters most to the decision?
alternative.alt_text: Consumer option comparison showing commitment, risk, flexibility and information gaps.

sections.learning_purpose: Define a workplace issue in neutral, researchable terms.
sections.watch_for: What makes this an issue rather than a single unsupported allegation?

alternative.before: Choose a teacher-provided contemporary issue topic.
alternative.during: Define scope, affected groups, observable indicators and key terms.
alternative.after: Write one neutral inquiry question and one boundary on the claim.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What evidence would be needed before drawing a conclusion?
alternative.alt_text: Neutral workplace issue definition with scope, indicators and evidence needs.

sections.learning_purpose: Compare evidence quality, impacts and perspectives.
sections.watch_for: Which claim is directly supported, and which is an inference?

alternative.before: Use two teacher-provided or current public sources.
alternative.during: Record claim, evidence, perspective, limitation and affected group.
alternative.after: State one supported conclusion and one remaining uncertainty.
alternative.evidence_prompt: How did the second source change your analysis?
alternative.alt_text: Matrix comparing workplace-issue evidence, perspectives, impacts and limitations.

sections.section_title: Responding through policy, support and action
sections.learning_purpose: Build a proportionate response pathway that includes current-authority checks.
sections.watch_for: Which step requires current policy or professional advice rather than classroom inference?

alternative.before: Read a fictional issue and identify immediate support needs.
alternative.during: Sequence clarify, record, verify, seek support, act and review.
alternative.after: Identify each current-policy or local-procedure point that must be checked against current teacher instructions.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which verification step prevents the largest unsupported assumption?
alternative.alt_text: Workplace issue response flowchart with support, verification and review steps.

sections.section_title: From strengths and needs to a viable idea
sections.learning_purpose: Distinguish a genuine need from a preferred solution and test fit with available strengths.
sections.watch_for: What evidence shows the need exists independently of the proposed idea?

alternative.before: Read a fictional user statement or conduct a consented classroom interview.
alternative.during: Separate need, evidence, strengths, limits and assumptions.
alternative.after: Revise the idea or record why it should not proceed yet.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What changed after listening to the need?
alternative.alt_text: Canvas connecting evidence of need with strengths, limits and assumptions.

sections.learning_purpose: Recognise that an enterprise model depends on resources, obligations, demand and risk.
sections.watch_for: Which assumption could make the model unworkable even if the idea is popular?

alternative.before: Read a fictional micro-enterprise outline.
alternative.during: Sort value, resources, revenue logic, obligations, risks and current-source checks.
alternative.after: Rank the two assumptions that need testing first.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What evidence would trigger continue, change or stop?
alternative.alt_text: Micro-enterprise model sorted by value, resources, obligations, risks and evidence checks.

sections.section_title: Planning, communicating and reviewing a micro-enterprise
sections.learning_purpose: Communicate a concise proposal and convert feedback into a review decision.
sections.watch_for: Which evidence should determine whether the idea continues, changes or stops?

alternative.before: Summarise need, value, user, resources, risk and test evidence.
alternative.during: Draft one clear frame for each element.
alternative.after: Use two feedback questions to record continue, change or stop.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which feedback point changed the proposal most?
alternative.alt_text: Six-frame micro-enterprise pitch ending in an evidence-based review decision.

sections.section_title: Defining the problem and project purpose
sections.learning_purpose: Turn a broad problem into a shared purpose, boundaries and observable criteria.
sections.watch_for: Which phrase defines the need without jumping straight to a solution?

alternative.before: Use a teacher-approved project context.
alternative.during: Define who, need, purpose, boundaries and three observable criteria.
alternative.after: Check each criterion against the purpose rather than effort alone.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which criterion best proves that the purpose was met?
alternative.alt_text: Project canvas defining need, purpose, boundaries and observable success criteria.

sections.section_title: Planning roles, resources, risks and communication
sections.learning_purpose: Coordinate roles, resources, risk checks and communication around a shared plan.
sections.watch_for: Where does one task depend on another role or a confirmed resource?

alternative.before: List the teacher-approved project tasks and available roles.
alternative.during: Map owner, dependency, resource, risk check and communication point.
alternative.after: Flag every local practical or safety detail that must be checked against current teacher instructions.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which dependency is most likely to delay the plan, and how will the team check it?
alternative.alt_text: Project planning board linking roles, dependencies, resources, checks and communication.

sections.section_title: Delivering, evaluating and presenting enterprise evidence
sections.learning_purpose: Select evidence that connects delivery decisions to project criteria and evaluation.
sections.watch_for: Which evidence proves a result against a criterion rather than merely showing activity?

alternative.before: Select one criterion, one evidence item and one project change.
alternative.during: Explain claim, evidence, decision and effect.
alternative.after: Add one limitation and one next improvement.
alternative.evidence_prompt: What does the evidence prove, and what can it not prove?
alternative.alt_text: Project evidence storyboard linking criterion, evidence, decision, effect and limitation.

sections.learning_purpose: Prepare communication and clarification without inventing placement procedures.
sections.watch_for: Which detail must come from the teacher or approved workplace information rather than this course site?

alternative.before: Use the generic introduction and clarification prompts.
alternative.during: Rehearse repeat-back, a question when unsure and the agreed contact route.
alternative.after: Identify every placement-specific requirement that must be checked against current teacher instructions.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which question would most reduce misunderstanding?
alternative.alt_text: Generic workplace preparation rehearsal with placement details marked for confirmation.

sections.learning_purpose: Record a de-identified observation and separate it from interpretation.
sections.watch_for: What did you directly observe, and what are you inferring from it?

alternative.before: Use an authorised observation, simulation or supplied case.
alternative.during: Record what happened, context, interpretation and a question without names.
alternative.after: Remove any claim that would require teacher observation to verify.
alternative.evidence_prompt: Which sentence is observation, and which is interpretation?
alternative.alt_text: De-identified workplace observation log separating fact, interpretation and question.

sections.section_title: Reflecting, transferring learning and planning next steps
sections.learning_purpose: Transfer one learning point from experience to another context and plan how to test it.
sections.watch_for: What changed in your understanding, and where could you test that learning next?

alternative.before: Select one de-identified observation or simulation moment.
alternative.during: Move from observation to interpretation, question and transferable skill.
alternative.after: Plan a realistic next context and evidence check.
alternative.evidence_prompt: How will you know whether the learning transferred?
alternative.alt_text: Reflection ladder linking workplace observation to a transferable skill and next test.
